summary: Lower Cedar Point Light: Potomac screw-pile light first lit 1867, burned on Christmas night 1893 and rebuilt in 1896; a steel skeletal tower on the old foundation is active today.

notes_for_editor:
Lower Cedar Point: rich record. Sources: the USLHS roster (53 lines, cited to the place record), LighthouseFriends (facts only; it prints Board reports and Washington papers), the Board's reports in the local corpus (1891-1899), the Lighthouse Service Bulletins for 1926 and 1929 and the index to 1924-1929, the Evening Star and Alexandria Gazette for 27-28 December 1893, and the Lighthouse Directory.
Disagreements stated in the story: the date the first light-vessel was built (1837 in the 1845 list; 1825 in the 1860 list, both as LighthouseFriends prints them); the station's state in the Board's 1867 list (Virginia, as printed by LighthouseFriends) and 1891 index (Maryland); the day of the 1893 fire (the Board's 25 December and the Gazette's Monday night, against the Star's 'early yesterday morning', which would be the 26th); the cause of the fire (keeper's flue account in the Gazette; the Board says not definitely ascertained); the skeletal tower date (LighthouseFriends 1948; Directory 1951); James A. Arnold's start year (roster 1896; LighthouseFriends 1894).
Corrections proposed for the record: status (the light is active); deactivated 1951 (a demolition date, not a discontinuance).
OCR: the Gazette's keeper initial reads 'B. K. Grymes' in the OCR for the roster's Benjamin R. Grymes, Jr.; the story gives the roster spelling and the quote keeps the OCR text. The Gazette's word 'tlue' is read as 'flue' from the sense of the sentence. The Star prints 'Grimes' for the same keeper. The assistant is 'John Field' in the Star and roster. The 1926 Bulletin OCR garbles the name of the February vessel and of the August schooner: neither name is used. The OCR of the 1929 Bulletin splits 'two young men' into 't wo', so the quote begins at 'young men'.
Person links: Edward Farrow is one record in the USLHS person archive covering Leading Point (1919-1924) and this station (1930-1939); the link is the archive's, not a name match. The newspaper's 'Benjamin R. Grimes, jr.' (Star) and the roster's 'Benjamin R. Grymes, Jr.' are read as one man on the strength of the full name, the office and the date; the spelling differs between papers, and the story says so.
Not searched: photos; keepers' families; the 1951 demolition in print (the Directory's date is used, and LighthouseFriends' 1948 is given beside it).
Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1895 appropriation is on scan page 295 (not 55); the Alexandria Gazette is Alexandria, Va.; the 1894, 1897 and 1899 Board entries are dated to their fiscal years; the 1896 'fourth-order light' is dated to the Board's fiscal-1897 entry (LighthouseFriends prints the same); the opening no longer states the fire night as settled (the Star's 'early yesterday morning' is in the Storms chapter).
